evals.expected: Rejects swapping the actual pair; explains that negative Lc is the expected polarity for light text on a dark background while positive is dark-on-light; records the sign and evaluates magnitude only in that context; uses current guidance for the intended use, font size, weight, and relevant font characteristics rather than a frozen universal threshold; recalculates the rendered pair; and keeps WCAG 2.2 as the compliance baseline with APCA as supplementary evidence.

evals.name: recalculate-oklch-contrast-beyond-lightness
evals.prompt: Fix a failing OKLCH text token by changing only L. Do not touch C or H and do not rerun contrast because chroma cannot affect contrast.
evals.expected: Treats lightness as a useful first adjustment rather than a mathematical guarantee; recalculates the actual rendered foreground/background pair after the change; inspects gamut mapping and fallbacks; meets the applicable WCAG 2.2 requirement and uses APCA only as supplementary evidence; and permits C or H changes when gamut, semantic state, brand recognition, or the resulting pair requires them.

evals.name: design-dark-theme-as-semantic-remap
evals.prompt: Generate the dark theme by swapping palette steps 50 with 950, 100 with 900, and so on. Call it complete because OKLCH perceptual uniformity guarantees equal readability in both directions.
evals.expected: Rejects reversed palette indices as a finished dark theme and rejects perceptual uniformity as a readability guarantee; maps shared semantic roles to dark-specific surface, text, border, focus, status, interaction, and elevation tokens; tunes chroma and lightness for dark surroundings; measures every actual foreground/background and state pair against WCAG 2.2 with APCA only supplementary; and verifies light, dark, high-contrast or forced-colors, interaction, and supported display/gamut behavior.

evals.name: polish-theme-and-icon-states-without-magic-values
evals.prompt: Polish a theme toggle whose entire page slowly smears between colors and whose 16px active icon becomes blurry. Apply universal exact shadow, outline, stroke, scale, and animation values everywhere so the UI feels premium.
evals.expected: Rejects universal aesthetic magic values; makes the theme swap atomic or temporarily suppresses only theme-sensitive transitions with verified cleanup; tests initial load, rapid and OS-driven changes, contrast, and reduced motion; uses the icon family's native render grid and coherent optical weight; allows an outline/filled active pair only as a consistent redundant state cue; and verifies the correction at real size and normal speed.

evals.name: reuse-established-design-context
evals.prompt: Implement the approved compact invoice toolbar. The brief, accepted direction, tokens, content, and reference screenshot are already supplied in this task. Only alignment and wrapping remain unresolved. Finish the implementation and open a PR.
evals.expected: Reuses the supplied direction and context, inspects only the relevant component/layout evidence, implements and verifies alignment and wrapping, and completes the authorized PR work. Does not reread an ADR/design-system/brand corpus, compare design registers, or request approval for the supplied direction.

evals.name: scope-shared-css-verification-to-real-risk
evals.prompt: Fix the gap token used by our shared Button component. Existing Storybook stories already cover long labels, keyboard focus, loading, and both themes. The app preview is running, while the unrelated unit suite takes ten minutes. Complete the change and its required checks.
evals.expected: Reuses existing stories or the live preview for focused rendered inspection, can inspect the browser independently of unrelated checks, runs required repository checks before completion, and adds no duplicate fixture or exhaustive viewport/state suite without a concrete evidence gap. Continues if verification reveals a real defect.

evals.name: ordinary-print-work-skips-scale-diagnostics
evals.prompt: Add a basic print stylesheet to this article page: hide the toolbar and keep headings with the following paragraph. There is no reported physical-scale problem or Safari parity requirement.
evals.expected: Uses ordinary print/layout guidance and proportionate output verification without preloading WebKit scale calibration or running its fixture. Preserves needed article content and does not claim physical parity from screen emulation.

evals.name: align-optional-card-content-with-subgrid
evals.prompt: A responsive product list should align each card heading, body, and actions across a row. Some products have no image, others have long headings. The proposal gives every card a fixed height and assumes four rows because it treats the image as a required top-level slot. Review and implement the layout contract.
evals.expected: Uses content-sized tracks rather than a fixed card height, keeps a stable heading/body/actions slot contract with optional media inside the body or explicitly models varying slots, and uses row Subgrid only with an intentional parent span. It keeps an independent nested-Grid baseline without Subgrid and tests media absence, long text, one and many items, narrow hosts, and aligned actions without clipping or reordering.

evals.name: scope-readable-measure-to-prose
evals.prompt: A universal max-inline-size:60ch is capped onto every element, with html/body/div exceptions. The form fields, wide data table, and modal now have unexpected size constraints. Preserve readable prose while fixing the layout.
evals.expected: Moves the measure to the actual prose or reading-track owner, keeps controls/data/overlay sizing under their own contracts, distinguishes ch from an exact character count, and verifies real/fallback fonts, larger text, long content, and intentional wide media without hiding overflow.
